event_confirmation: Company release of 2026-10-08: FQ1 FY27 results after market close Thursday 2026-10-22, call 4:30pm ET (https://www.westerndigital.com/company/newsroom/press-releases/2026/2026-10-08-wd-to-announce-first-quarter-fiscal-year-2027-financial-results). Session amc confirmed.
conviction_note: Fundamentals lean to a modest beat (guide $4.1B/$4.00 is below consensus ~$4.15B/$4.07-4.11, BofA checks $4.22B/$4.29, CFO said in September GM keeps rising), and the stock is -22% in 20 days and ~-7% intraday into the print on the Toshiba-capacity scare, but this name has sold its last three beats (-13.0%, -0.7%, -10.1%) and the 25d skew is +11 vol points of put demand, so the lean in p_up is only 52 against an abs move of 9%; the findings sum (+0.6) and the scaled number (+0.36) agree in sign and size.
bar: Revenue: company guide $4.1B +/- $0.1B, non-GAAP EPS $4.00 +/- $0.15, GM 55-56% (8-K ex-99.1, 2026-08-05, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000106040/000162828026053305/a4ex991-pressreleaseq426.htm). Consensus sits above the guide midpoint: Zacks EPS $4.07, Benzinga $4.03-4.04 / revenue $4.14B (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/WDC/earnings-forecasts), other previews $4.10-4.11 / $4.15-4.16B (https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262232325-stock-western-digital-wdc-price-prediction-tradingkey). BofA above the street at $4.22B / $4.29 / GM 56.4% (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/bofa-lifts-western-digital-target-023300215.html). The real bar is the December-quarter guide (GM trajectory vs Seagate's mid-57% Sept-quarter guide) and any LTA/pricing update answering the Toshiba capacity worry. print_vs_bar_pct is measured on revenue vs ~$4.15B.
positioning_check: Short interest 18.3M shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement (up from 17.3M), 2.45 days to cover, roughly 5% of float (https://www.optionsanalysissuite.com/stocks/wdc/short-interest) - not crowded, no squeeze mechanism. Skew_25d +11.14 vol points (downside paid), ATM IV 125%, straddle 7.38%, put/call OI 0.63. Tape: -22.1% over 20 days, -53% from the 52-week high (record close $746.23 on 2026-06-18), spot $350.67 at 17:08 UTC on the print day against a $378.51 close on 10-21, i.e. about -7% intraday into the release. Wells Fargo cut its target $730 -> $450 on 10-16 (Overweight kept); BofA raised to $800 on 10-21.

findings.finding: BofA (Wamsi Mohan, 2026-10-21) models FQ1 revenue $4.22B, EPS $4.29 and GM 56.4%, above both the company guide ($4.1B / $4.00 / 55-56%) and consensus ($4.16B / $4.11), says its industry checks show no pricing pressure from the Toshiba expansion and calls hyperscaler pricing talks 'constructive'; it cut its exabyte growth assumption to 21% y/y while lifting price/TB to +24% y/y.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: WDC beat in each of the last three prints and fell -10.1% (Jan-26), -0.7% (Apr-26) and -13.0% (Aug-26; EPS $3.56 vs $3.31, revenue $3.75B vs $3.70B, guide above consensus). Beats on the reported quarter have been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a published sell-side note, so the number is partly priced; the stock rose +3.9% on it on 10-21 and then gave all of that back and more (~-7%) on 10-22 before the print, so the market is not paying for a beat - a priced beat would show the stock holding the 10-21 gain and skew easing, not +11 vol points of put demand.
findings.independence: Same direction from the company's own guide-vs-consensus gap (guide midpoint $4.1B below a ~$4.15B consensus; last quarter's revenue beat the guide midpoint) in the 8-K at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000106040/000162828026053305/a4ex991-pressreleaseq426.htm.

findings.finding: CFO Kris Sennesael at Citi's TMT conference (2026-09-09, mid-quarter): GM in the mid-50s 'should keep rising' with no ceiling he can see, price/TB up 18-19% y/y last quarter with 'a little bit more room there to grow', the vast majority of calendar-2027 volume already under LTAs, 52-week lead times, revenue gated by supply not demand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: August 2026: Q1 guide was above revenue consensus but GM 55-56% was ~200bp below Seagate's mid-57% and the stock fell -13.0%; the guide's margin line, not revenue, is what was punished last time.
findings.why_not_priced: Said publicly six weeks ago, but since then the stock has fallen ~50% from its high on a supply-side (Toshiba) scare that does not touch calendar-2027 pricing already set in LTAs; if the market were pricing a continued GM ramp into the December-quarter guide, the stock would not be at the April low with puts bid.
findings.independence: BofA expects December-quarter GM approaching 59% (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/bofa-lifts-western-digital-target-023300215.html); Wells Fargo sees a path to 60-65% GM (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/Markets/Equity/wdc-stx-stocks-headed-for-third-straight-weekly-loss-wells-fargo-slashes-targets-but-sees-opportunity/cZxKGWBRBs9).

findings.finding: At the same Citi conference the CFO flagged near-term DRAM and NAND cost headwinds - a component-cost item that could cap the GM step in the December-quarter guide while memory prices are rising.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August print was sold on a margin guide that disappointed versus Seagate (-13.0%).
findings.why_not_priced: No preview or sell-side note found mentions memory BOM cost for WDC; consensus GM views (BofA 56.4%, ~59% Dec-Q) assume clean expansion. If priced, previews would carry a GM haircut for memory costs. DRAM/NAND are a small share of an HDD bill of materials, so the size is small.
findings.independence: Same document as the finding above (one transcript read two ways, one bullish line and one bearish line); no second source for the cost headwind found.

findings.finding: Exabyte shipments are supply-capped below the 25% target: Q4 FY26 231EB +22% y/y (CFO: 22-23%), and BofA cut its FQ1 exabyte growth estimate to 21%; volume, not price, is the line that can disappoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Exabyte growth below the 25% target was part of the August print that fell -13.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: Known since August; the specific risk is that sub-25% bit growth on the call reads as share loss to Seagate's HAMR at a moment when the market is worried about new supply - the market has priced supply risk from Toshiba but the BofA cut to 21% is two days old.
findings.independence: BofA estimate cut to 21% (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/bofa-lifts-western-digital-target-023300215.html), a different source from the transcript.

findings.finding: The call is the first chance for management to answer the Toshiba capacity scare (Nikkei 2026-10-02: Toshiba to double HDD capacity for AI data centres by its fiscal 2027, i.e. from April 2027, ~$380M investment) with LTA news: management said in August it is 'in the throes of' negotiating LTAs for calendar 2029-2031 and in September that customers want contracts to 2030-31 but 'we haven't signed them yet'; a signed multi-year LTA disclosed tonight would directly rebut the supply-glut thesis behind the 18-22% drawdown.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print has carried an LTA-signing announcement; the August print with LTA commentary but no signing fell -13.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: The October drawdown was attributed to Toshiba supply (Wells Fargo cut targets on 'pricing power' fears; Morgan Stanley called it multiple-driven, not earnings). If the market were pricing contracted pricing to 2029+, the stock would not have re-tested its April low at $330 on 10-19 with +11 vol points of put skew. Whether a signing is announced tonight is uncertain, which is why the range runs negative too (no signing plus soft December-quarter GM).
findings.independence: Citi (2026-10-02) said the market overstates Toshiba's impact because Toshiba depends on outside suppliers for heads and media (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/seagate-tumbles-10-western-digital-125250923.html); BofA's checks show no pricing pressure (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/bofa-lifts-western-digital-target-023300215.html).

findings.finding: Reaction function: WDC fell after each of its last three prints despite beats (-10.1%, -0.7%, -13.0%), and in August a guide above revenue consensus still produced -13.0% and a sector sell-off; the market's habit on this name is to sell the release.
findings.why_not_priced: The three sell-offs came off record highs after big run-ups (August: ~+200% YTD into the print); this time the stock is -49% from its record close, so part of the sell-the-news mechanism may be spent. Filed small because the skew already prices downside.
findings.independence: Baseline history (sealed file) shows the same three negative reactions; same direction as the +11 vol-point put skew.

findings.finding: Expectations have been reset into the print: -22% over 20 days, -49% from the $746 record close, a re-test of the $330 April low on 10-19, Wells Fargo cutting its target from $730 to $450 on 10-16, and roughly -7% intraday on 10-22 on a sector de-rating (weak NAND/PC demand, memory names sold) that does not touch nearline HDD; Morgan Stanley called the ~18% sell-off multiple-driven, not an earnings collapse.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last five prints that came in after a period without a big run-up (Jan-25 to Oct-25) all rose (+1.2% to +10.2%); the three sold prints came after big run-ups.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is the price itself, so this is a lean, not a fact the market lacks; it is sized small and against a strong put skew because the option market is explicitly paying for further downside and pre-print run-ups have not predicted direction in this repo's sample.
findings.independence: Intraday decline and reasons (NAND/PC weakness, sector deleveraging): https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262232325-stock-western-digital-wdc-price-prediction-tradingkey (2026-10-22); Morgan Stanley 'multiple-driven' via https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9108148/western-digital-wdc-shares-plunge-over-10-amid-sector-selloff-on-october-2-2026 search context and the invezz 10-20 headline (not fetchable, 403).

findings.finding: Independent price series: eRacks' six-month tracking (published 2026-09-14) shows enterprise HDD prices up through August with nothing falling - Toshiba MG enterprise +38% and Seagate Exos SATA +15% per TB from March to August - consistent with continued price/TB gains in WDC's September quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Price/TB has risen in each recent quarter (high single digits to high teens y/y); the market sold the last two prints anyway.
findings.why_not_priced: A retail/channel proxy that no preview cites; nearline is priced under LTAs, so the channel series is a weak proxy for WDC's hyperscale pricing and is sized accordingly. If the market priced continued pricing gains it would not be selling the group on a 2027-dated capacity plan.
findings.independence: Proxy; the company's own statement (price/TB high-teens y/y, more room to grow) points the same way: https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/western-digital-at-citis-2026-global-tmt-conference-cloud-demand-drives-shift-93CH-4893849.

findings.finding: Peer margin gap: Seagate guided its September quarter to a non-GAAP GM around mid-57% while WDC guided 55-56%; Seagate reports on 2026-10-27, after this window, so WDC's December-quarter GM guide will be compared against Seagate's previous trajectory with no fresh peer datapoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: August 2026: the ~200bp GM gap to Seagate was cited for the -13.0% reaction.
findings.source_date: 2026-07 (Seagate Q4 FY26 call read-through, as shown on the post)
findings.why_not_priced: The gap itself is old and priced; what is not known is whether WDC narrows it in the December-quarter guide. Filed small because it is an inference from a peer.
findings.independence: Seagate report date confirmed for 2026-10-27: https://finviz.com/news/402052/seagate-technology-to-report-fiscal-first-quarter-2027-financial-results-on-october-27-2026; the GM gap as the August sell-off driver: https://www.itiger.com/news/1199953755.

findings.finding: Financing: WDC exchanged ~$191.0M of its 3.00% 2028 converts on 2026-08-26 for ~$192.7M cash plus shares for the conversion value above principal, and on 2026-09-14 called the remaining $109.5M for redemption on 2026-11-16 (conversion rate 26.5231 shares per $1,000, principal in cash, excess in shares); the money retires debt into a net-cash balance sheet, and the share effect (low single-digit millions of shares against ~388M diluted) is largely already in the if-converted diluted count.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to earlier Sandisk-stake debt-for-equity exchanges at prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed in 8-Ks; it is a deleveraging, not distress, and moves the share count marginally. Sized at zero after asking what the money buys: debt retirement on a net-cash balance sheet.
findings.independence: Redemption notice 8-K ex-99.1, 2026-09-14: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/106040/000119312526389859/d23939dex991.htm (same issuer, separate filing).

findings.finding: Capital return: $3.26B of buyback authorization remained at 2026-07-03 (10-K), WDC is net cash after monetizing Sandisk, management says most FCF goes to buybacks and more dividend increases are planned; with the stock ~50% below its June peak, the FQ1 buyback figure and any dividend raise or new authorization reported tonight are a possible support.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The February 2026 $4.0B authorization was announced alongside a print that fell -10.1%; capital return has not carried a print on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is public; what is not public is the pace bought in a quarter where the stock fell from ~$520 to ~$400. A priced expectation of an accelerated buyback would show in less put demand.
findings.independence: CFO on FCF to buybacks and planned dividend increases (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/western-digital-at-citis-2026-global-tmt-conference-cloud-demand-drives-shift-93CH-4893849); Q4 FY26 buybacks $672M (8-K ex-99.1).

findings.finding: Insider: a Form 144 filed 2026-10-21 for officer Cynthia Lock Tregillis proposes selling 807 shares (about $0.3M), the day before the print - immaterial in size.
findings.why_not_priced: Too small to matter; filed for completeness.

outside_window.finding: Seagate reports FQ1 FY27 on 2026-10-27 after the close - the direct peer read-through (nearline pricing, GM, Toshiba commentary) lands after this window.
Remaining $109.5M of 2028 convertibles redeemed 2026-11-16 (conversion deadline 2026-11-12); share settlement of the excess conversion value happens after the window.

Toshiba's doubled HDD capacity arrives in its fiscal 2027 (April 2027 onward); actual supply effect on nearline pricing is far outside the window, only the narrative is inside it (filed above as the LTA finding).

baseline_tension: The small positive lean cuts against the +11 vol-point put skew and the three-print sell-the-beat habit, and agrees with nothing in the tape except that the 20-day drawdown has lowered the bar; that tension is why p_up is 52, not higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold its last three beats): BofA reported-quarter beat finding cut +0.8 -> +0.4; CFO GM/pricing guidance finding cut +0.8 -> +0.6; p_up 54 -> 52.
Lesson 7 (sign against a strong skew needs a reason): de-rating/positioning lean cut +0.7 -> +0.3, since the +11 vol-point put skew explicitly pays for further downside.
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): LTA-signing finding cut +1.0 -> +0.7 because the CFO said on 09-09 'we haven't signed them yet'.
Lesson 5 (proxy loses to broad series): eRacks channel-price proxy cut +0.3 -> +0.2.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): convert exchange/redemption checked - debt retirement on a net-cash balance sheet, left at 0.0.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar, keep inside window): bar sourced to company guide plus Zacks/Benzinga consensus; Seagate print, convert redemption and Toshiba capacity date kept in outside_window. No size change from this.
